variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: ML systems design is the work of turning a prediction problem into a dependable product capability. It connects data collection, feature computation, model training, evaluation, deployment, serving, monitoring, and feedback so that a useful decision reaches a user under real constraints.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Decision
pairs.detail: Name who consumes the prediction and what they do with it.
pairs.explanation: Name who consumes the prediction and what they do with it. A risk score used to block a payment has different failure costs from a score used to order a review queue.

pairs.label: Evidence
pairs.detail: List features that legally and technically exist at prediction time.
pairs.explanation: List features that legally and technically exist at prediction time. Historical correlations are not usable if they arrive after the decision.

pairs.label: Service promise
pairs.detail: Set freshness, latency, throughput, availability, privacy, and cost targets.
pairs.explanation: Set freshness, latency, throughput, availability, privacy, and cost targets. Use percentiles and peak traffic rather than averages alone.

pairs.label: Failure policy
pairs.detail: Define fallback, abstention, human review, and rollback behavior before deployment.
pairs.explanation: Define fallback, abstention, human review, and rollback behavior before deployment. A model timeout must not invent product policy.

variants.hint:
Decision: Name who consumes the prediction and what they do with it.

Evidence: List features that legally and technically exist at prediction time.

Service promise: Set freshness, latency, throughput, availability, privacy, and cost targets.

Failure policy: Define fallback, abstention, human review, and rollback behavior before deployment.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

pairs.detail: Compare candidates against the baseline on representative time periods, slices, calibration, robustness, and resource use.

pairs.label: Release with containment

pairs.explanation: Use shadow traffic, canaries, fallbacks, immutable artifacts, and automatic rollback conditions to limit exposure.

pairs.label: Observe outcomes and adapt

pairs.explanation: Join predictions, decisions, exposures, and delayed outcomes; detect drift; then retrain only from validated evidence.

variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: ML systems design is the work of turning a prediction problem into a dependable product capability. It connects data collection, feature computation, model training, evaluation, deployment, serving, monitoring, and feedback so that a useful decision reaches a user under real constraints.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Scheduled batch
pairs.detail: Score many entities on a schedule and store the results.
pairs.explanation: Score many entities on a schedule and store the results. This is simple and efficient when the product accepts predictions that are minutes or hours old.

pairs.label: Request-time online
pairs.detail: Fetch eligible features and run inference while the user waits.
pairs.explanation: Fetch eligible features and run inference while the user waits. This supports live context but consumes the request latency and availability budget.

pairs.label: Hybrid
pairs.detail: Precompute expensive candidates or features, then use fresh context to filter or rerank online.
pairs.explanation: Precompute expensive candidates or features, then use fresh context to filter or rerank online. The added path is justified only when both scale and freshness demand it.

variants.hint:

Request-time online: Fetch eligible features and run inference while the user waits.

Hybrid: Precompute expensive candidates or features, then use fresh context to filter or rerank online.

variants.title: Give each part its job

It connects data collection, feature computation, model training, evaluation, deployment, serving, monitoring, and feedback so that a useful decision reaches a user under real constraints.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Replay
pairs.detail: Test a time-based holdout, critical slices, calibration, robustness, latency, and cost against the current production baseline.
pairs.explanation: Test a time-based holdout, critical slices, calibration, robustness, latency, and cost against the current production baseline.

pairs.label: Shadow
pairs.detail: Run the candidate on production inputs without affecting decisions.
pairs.explanation: Run the candidate on production inputs without affecting decisions. Compare feature parity, outputs, latency, and resource demand.

pairs.label: Canary
pairs.detail: Expose a small, representative cohort with guardrails for quality, latency, errors, safety, and business harm.
pairs.explanation: Expose a small, representative cohort with guardrails for quality, latency, errors, safety, and business harm.

pairs.label: Promote or roll back
pairs.detail: Increase traffic only when predeclared checks pass.
pairs.explanation: Increase traffic only when predeclared checks pass. Keep the prior artifact and routing policy ready for immediate restoration.

variants.hint:
Replay: Test a time-based holdout, critical slices, calibration, robustness, latency, and cost against the current production baseline.

Shadow: Run the candidate on production inputs without affecting decisions.

Canary: Expose a small, representative cohort with guardrails for quality, latency, errors, safety, and business harm.

Promote or roll back: Increase traffic only when predeclared checks pass.
